title: PICSP3D: a parallel three-dimensional electrostatic particle-in-cell code for plasma-object interaction
description:
PICSP3D is an open-source, three-dimensional, three-velocity (3D3V) electrostatic particle-in-cell code for plasma-object interaction, such as spacecraft and probe charging, sheaths and wakes, Langmuir probes, dust grains, electrodes, magnetised plasma devices and gas discharges.

Objects of arbitrary shape are embedded in a uniform Cartesian grid as signed distance functions, built from analytic primitives with constructive solid geometry or imported from CAD (STL) with generalised winding numbers. The Poisson equation is solved with a multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient method and second-order Shortley-Weller cut cells; floating and biased conductors are charged self-consistently through a capacitance matrix. The code includes surface processes (absorption, secondary electron emission, photoemission with self-shadowing), uniform and spatially varying static magnetic fields (dipoles, current loops, solenoids, mirrors, wires) with a Boris pusher, Monte Carlo collisions with a neutral background (elastic, charge exchange, excitation, ionisation) and binary Coulomb collisions.

The solver is written in C++20 and parallelised with MPI domain decomposition and OpenMP threads; output is parallel VTK. A Python package, picsp_post, provides post-processing, figures, animations, Blender renders and a CAD import tool. The release contains the test suite, sixteen documented example cases with analysis scripts, the scaling benchmark and its results.
